headline: Ministry of Earth Sciences Celebrates 20th Foundation Day, Highlighting Two Decades of Scientific Excellence and National Service
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

Ministry of Earth Sciences Celebrates 20th Foundation Day, Highlighting Two Decades of Scientific Excellence and National Service

27 JUL 2026 10:40PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES) celebrated its momentous 20th Foundation Day at Prithvi Bhawan, New Delhi, marking two decades of pioneering contributions to earth systems science, weather forecasting, oceanography, and polar research. The grand event witnessed the convergence of eminent scientific leaders, policymakers, and researchers from across the nation.

Highlights and Address by MoES Secretary, Dr N. Kalaiselvi

The celebration was graced by Dr N. Kalaiselvi, Secretary, MoES, who presided over the function. In her inspiring presidential address, Dr. Kalaiselvi warmly congratulated the MoES family on reaching this crucial milestone, emphasised that the ministry has grown into an indispensable pillar for the nation, acting as a complete value chain: "You (the Ministry) are the data provider through Prithvi systems, you are the service provider through Mission Mausam, and you are the technology provider through your deep ocean mission."

Highlighting the unique integration of scientific bodies under MoES, she drew attention to the synergy between the 20-year-old ministry and its legendary 150+ year-old constituent, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), remarking that it exemplifies true youth-and-experience harmony and total commitment without hierarchical barriers.

Dr Kalaiselvi also paid glowing tributes to the Guests of Honour, noting that the presence of veteran pioneers like Dr A.E. Muthunayagam and Dr Chandramouli Gaddamanugu bridges the legacy of visionary architects like Dr Vikram Sarabhai and Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam with contemporary earth sciences.

Distinguished Dignitaries and Attendees & their Insights

The event featured distinguished Guests of Honour:

Dr A.E. Muthunayagam (Padma Shri awardee and the founding Director/Secretary of the Department of Ocean Development (DOD), erstwhile the Ministry of Earth Sciences) took the audience down memory lane, tracing the genesis of ocean research in India back to July 1981 with the establishment of the Department of Ocean Development under the Prime Minister's direct purview. He detailed the expansion of India’s maritime and polar footprint—from launching the maiden Antarctic expedition from Goa in 1981, establishing permanent research stations like Dakshin Gangotri, Maitri, and Bharati, to setting up key autonomous institutions such as NIOT, NCAOR (now NCPOR), and INCOIS, as well as advancing ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) and desalination technologies for the blue economy.

Dr Chandramouli Gaddamanugu (Padma Shri awardee & eminent defence scientist and veteran leader of the Akash missile development Program) reflected on his decades of formative mentorship under Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam during the development of the indigenous Akash missile system. Drawing parallels between defense preparedness and earth systems science, he underscored the importance of indigenous innovation, multi-disciplinary team integration, absolute elimination of organizational egos, and rigorous validation in overcoming technical challenges to serve national security and societal resilience.

The occasion also saw the prominent presence of Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, Director General of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), and Shri Sreenivasa Rao Gangi Reddy, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences, alongside various directors of autonomous institutions, scientists, and administrative staff.

Releases and Launches

Aligned with its mission to enhance public service and operational efficiency, the 20th Foundation Day event featured the official release of key scientific reports and the launch of new technological applications to bolster early warning systems, disaster management, and weather-tracking capabilities across the country:

1. India Meteorological Department (IMD)

Centres of Excellence (CoEs): Establishment of 13 specialized CoEs across India (such as Desert Meteorology in Jaipur, Mountain Meteorology in Dehradun, Thunderstorm Research in Patna, and Agro-meteorological Research in Bengaluru).

Upgradation: Upgrading the Cyclone Warning Centre (CWC) in Thiruvananthapuram to an Area Cyclone Warning Centre (ACWC) to cover Kerala, Karnataka, and Lakshadweep.

Animal Disease Forecasting: A joint MoU between IMD and ICAR-NIVEDI to establish the Weather Driven Animal Disease Risk Forecasting Unit (WAADRU) for district-level livestock disease risk predictions up to two months in advance.

IMD NOVA: Launch of a web platform for tracking, validating, and archiving thunderstorm nowcasts using lightning network and AWS data.

2. National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF)

WINGS Mobile Application: A unified mobile platform providing numerical weather prediction, AI/ML predictions, and real-time mesoscale analysis.

National Doppler Weather Radar Reflectivity Mosaic: A seamless, near-real-time visualization tool developed under Mission Mausam to monitor convective systems and severe weather.

NCMRWF Open Data Portal: Redesigned portal offering expanded datasets, including subseasonal-to-seasonal hindcasts, multi-source ensemble rainfall analysis, and 10 years of operational ocean analysis using NEMOVAR.

3. National Centre for Seismology (NCS)

Compendium of Monthly Seismological Bulletins (2023 & 2024): Publication providing validated earthquake catalogues, phase data, and hypocentral parameters from the National Seismological Network (NSN).

Strong Motion Atlas of India (2010–2020): Compilation of strong ground-motion records and accelerograms for earthquakes of magnitude 4.0 and above to support earthquake engineering and hazard assessment.

4. Centre for Marine Living Resources and Ecology (CMLRE)

Taxonomic Manuals: Release of A Pictorial Identification Manual for Tintinnid Ciliates of the Eastern Arabian Sea covering 100 species, and Seamount-Associated Animals of the Indian EEZ (Part I: Lakshadweep Sea) documenting 225 species.

Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs): Documentation outlining guidelines for collecting, preserving, and processing marine biological samples using classical taxonomy, molecular systematics, and genomics.

5. National Centre for Coastal Research (NCCR)

Sagar Prahari App: An AI-enabled, citizen-centric mobile application for geo-tagging beach cleanups and automatically identifying marine litter.

SAHAV 2.0: An advanced open-source, GIS-based decision-support platform for Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) featuring geospatial analytics and Ocean Accounting modules.

6. National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT)

Infrastructure Dedication: Inauguration of the marine pipeline trestle, boat landing, and seawater intake facility for the Ballast Water Treatment Test Facility in Pamanji, Andhra Pradesh, along with an IoT-enabled nearshore Met-Ocean observatory.

Mariculture Demonstration: Deployment of 8 circular HDPE floating fish cages for open-sea cage culture of Asian seabass at Chidiyatappu, Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

Deep Sea Mining Outreach: Industry outreach initiatives targeted at exploring 75,000 sq. km in the Central Indian Ocean Basin containing polymetallic nodules.

Ocean Olympiad India 2026: A national-level multi-tier competition aimed at promoting ocean literacy among undergraduate students.

The celebration concluded with a renewed pledge from the entire MoES fraternity to push the frontiers of atmospheric, oceanic, polar, and cryospheric research, turning scientific knowledge into national wealth and societal safety.

headline: Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Announces Task Force to Support Toy Sector, Targets 5% Global Market Share by 2032
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Announces Task Force to Support Toy Sector, Targets 5% Global Market Share by 2032

Shri Piyush Goyal Launches Toy Sector Playbook to Strengthen Manufacturing, Innovation and Exports

Stakeholders Deliberate on Roadmap to Scale Up Manufacturing, Innovation and Exports in India's Toy Sector

27 JUL 2026 9:51PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today announced the setting up of a task force to support the toy sector and identify interventions towards achieving the goal of reaching a 5 per cent share in the global toy market by 2032. The announcement was made at the stakeholder meet, “Team Up for Toys: Driving SCALE, Innovation and Exports”, organised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi.

The task force will work towards achieving six objectives, namely, integration with global value chains, strengthening manufacturing capabilities, resolving value chain bottlenecks, creating skilled workforce and employment, enabling design and innovation, and enhancing ease of doing business.

The event brought together policymakers, industry leaders, manufacturers, startups, investors, artisans, designers and other key stakeholders from across the toy ecosystem to deliberate on the future growth trajectory of India's toy sector and marked the launch of the Toy Sector Playbook.

In his address, Shri Piyush Goyal stated that the remarkable progress of India's toy industry reflects the country's broader journey towards Viksit Bharat. Highlighting the sector's unique ability to combine manufacturing excellence, creativity, innovation and India's rich cultural heritage, he noted that Indian-made toys are increasingly reaching markets across the world. The Minister called upon industry stakeholders to work towards building a complete domestic manufacturing ecosystem supported by advanced technologies, globally competitive quality standards, deep localisation, stronger branding and greater integration with global value chains.

Shri Piyush Goyal subsequently launched the Toy Sector Playbook. Developed as a comprehensive roadmap for manufacturers, startups, MSMEs, investors and entrepreneurs, the Playbook provides actionable guidance on manufacturing ecosystems, value chains, standards and compliance requirements, skills development, product innovation, intellectual property, exports and emerging market opportunities. It aims to serve as a practical resource for stakeholders seeking to strengthen competitiveness and expand their presence in both domestic and international markets.

The Minister further highlighted the positive impact of various government initiatives, including quality regulation through BIS certification, cluster development programmes and support measures for MSMEs and startups. He urged industry to focus on innovation, design excellence, sustainability, scale and exports to create globally recognised Indian toy brands and establish India as a leading hub for toy design, manufacturing and exports.

Welcoming the participants, Joint Secretary, SCALE, DPIIT, Dr. Kajal highlighted the role of the Steering Committee for Advancing Local Value Add and Employment (SCALE) and the RAPiD Unit in advancing the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. She noted that the toy sector was among the earliest sectors identified for focused intervention owing to its strong potential for local value addition, employment generation and export growth. She further highlighted the rapid expansion of India's toy ecosystem, which today comprises more than 21,000 MSMEs, over 770 DPIIT-recognised toy startups, nearly 50 toy clusters and more than 1,800 BIS licensees.

Setting the context for the discussions, Chairman, SCALE, Dr. Pawan Goenka outlined the vision of transforming India into a global toy manufacturing powerhouse. He underscored the significant opportunity presented by the rapidly expanding global toy industry and noted that India is well positioned to emerge as a trusted manufacturing and export destination as global supply chains diversify. Highlighting the strong growth potential of the domestic market, he emphasised the aspiration of increasing India's share in the global toy market to 5 per cent by 2032 through enhanced scale, innovation, design capabilities and export competitiveness.

Following the launch, stakeholders participated in extensive deliberations. Discussions focused on scaling up manufacturing, strengthening local supply chains, enhancing design and innovation capabilities, improving quality standards, developing skilled manpower, promoting exports, attracting investments and increasing India's participation in global toy value chains.

The event concluded with a vote of thanks by Joint Secretary, DPIIT, Dr. Sumeet Jarangal, and reaffirmed the shared commitment of the Government and industry to ensure that the toys of the future are not only Made in India, but also Designed in India, Innovated in India, Branded in India and celebrated across the world.

headline: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting on MDoNER's Flagship USP Initiative
fullText:
Ministry of Development of North-East Region

Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting on MDoNER's Flagship USP Initiative

Advancing Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Vision of an Aatmanirbhar and Globally Competitive North East

27 JUL 2026 9:01PM by PIB Delhi

New Delhi, July 27, 2026- Union Minister for Development of North Eastern Region and Communications, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, today chaired the Parliamentary Consultative Committee meeting of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) to review the progress of the Ministry's flagship Unique Selling Proposition (USP) initiative. The meeting was attended by Minister of State for DoNER, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Members of Parliament representing all the Ashtalakshmi States, and senior officials of the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER).

The meeting witnessed a productive interaction with Members of Parliament, who shared valuable state-specific feedback, implementation experiences and suggestions to further strengthen project execution. Discussions focused on enhancing market access, value addition, branding, logistics, export promotion and institutional support while reinforcing coordination between the Centre and the States.

USP Initiative to Remain State-Driven

Shri Scindia emphasised that the USP initiative is fundamentally state-driven, with each State Government identifying its flagship product based on its comparative strengths and local aspirations. He stated that MDoNER's role is to facilitate convergence, coordinate with Central Ministries and State Governments, and bring together all stakeholders to accelerate implementation.

Whole-of-Government Approach Driving Convergence

Highlighting the Ministry's Whole-of-Government approach, the Minister said that MDoNER is acting as an aggregator by bringing together Central Ministries, State Governments, implementing agencies, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), industry partners, financial institutions and the private sector. He underlined that the flagship projects are being implemented through convergence of schemes and resources to maximise outcomes through collaborative action.

Building Globally Competitive Value Chains

The Minister reiterated that every flagship initiative has been designed around a complete market-linked development model with equal emphasis on production enhancement, quality improvement, processing infrastructure, branding, packaging, value addition and assured market linkages. He noted that the objective is not merely to increase production but to build globally competitive value chains capable of generating sustainable livelihoods for farmers, entrepreneurs and local communities.

Eight Flagship Missions Across the North East

The flagship initiatives currently being implemented include the Kiwi Mission in Arunachal Pradesh, Muga Silk Mission in Assam, Lakadong Turmeric Mission in Meghalaya, Ginger Mission in Mizoram, Coffee Mission in Nagaland, Organic Agriculture Mission in Sikkim and Queen Pineapple Mission in Tripura.

One Flagship Product Per State in the First Phase

The Minister informed the Committee that the Ministry's immediate strategy is to successfully establish one flagship product in each State before expanding to additional sectors in subsequent phases. He observed that product overlap across States is acceptable where a State possesses a distinct competitive advantage or market identity. Referring to Sikkim, Shri Scindia highlighted the State's unique position as India's only 100 per cent organic State, giving it a significant advantage in global markets.

Focus on Branding, Logistics and Export Readiness

The Committee also deliberated on measures to strengthen branding, logistics and export readiness. Members suggested promoting Northeast products through airports, Parliament outlets and dedicated marketing platforms. The Minister highlighted ongoing efforts to connect the region's premium products with international markets and major e-commerce platforms while strengthening value chains and processing infrastructure.

MPs Suggest Measures for Effective Implementation of Flagship Initiatives

Members of Parliament shared several constructive suggestions and discussed key aspects of implementation, including the need for additional technical manpower, expeditious approvals, stronger inter-ministerial coordination, enhanced support for certification and exports, and greater awareness and capacity building among farmers and producer groups.

Appreciating the valuable suggestions received from the Members, Shri Scindia encouraged them to continue acting as facilitators between the Centre and the States to ensure timely and effective implementation of the flagship initiatives.

The meeting reaffirmed the Ministry's commitment to transforming the unique strengths of every Ashtalakshmi State into globally competitive economic opportunities through quality production, value addition, robust logistics, strong market linkages and collaborative governance, in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of a prosperous, Aatmanirbhar and Viksit North East.

The Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, said that the welfare of humanity lies in the protection and respect of nature. He noted that India’s timeless traditions also inspire us to uphold this righteous way of life and live in harmony with the natural world.

Traction System Upgrade Over 164 Track Km to Handle Higher Freight Volumes and Support Running of Vande Bharat Express Trains

In a significant step towards strengthening railway infrastructure and enhancing network capacity, Indian Railways has sanctioned the upgradation of the electric traction system on the Parbhani-Mudkhed double line section in Nanded Division of South Central Railway. The project involves converting the existing 1x25 kV electric traction system to a more advanced 2x25 kV system over a stretch of 164 Track Kilometres, supported by upgraded power supply infrastructure to meet the enhanced electrical load.

The Parbhani-Mudkhed section forms part of the strategically important Highly Utilised Network (HUN) Route-9, connecting Ajmer-Indore-Khandwa-Akola-Purna-Mudkhed-Secunderabad-Mahbubnagar-Dhone.

The upgraded traction system will strengthen power supply for train operations, enabling the section to handle higher freight volumes and support the running of Vande Bharat Express trains. It will also contribute to Indian Railways' goal of achieving 3,000 Million Tonnes of freight loading by 2029-30.

The project reflects Indian Railways' continuing efforts to modernise electrical infrastructure and improve operational efficiency on high-density corridors across the country.

headline: Raksha Mantri unveils landmark policy reforms for ICG personnel & their families
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

Raksha Mantri unveils landmark policy reforms for ICG personnel & their families

28 JUL 2026 12:33PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has unveiled two significant policy reforms for the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) aimed at promoting gender parity in the induction & service conditions of officers, and streamlining the administrative procedures for granting ex-gratia to the families of personnel reported missing at sea while on duty. Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh, DG ICG Director General Paramesh Sivamani and other senior officials attended the event at Kartavya Bhavan-2, New Delhi on July 28, 2026.

Lauding the ICG for its exemplary service over the past five decades, Raksha Mantri exuded confidence that these forward-looking policies will further strengthen the morale and operational efficacy of the force as it marches toward its Swarnim Jayanti (Golden Jubilee) in 2027. He reaffirmed Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi-led Government’s resolve to strengthen the ICG as a modern, capable and future-ready maritime force.

Gender-neutral induction & career progression

The first policy directive establishes a comprehensive, women-centric approach by ushering in a gender-neutral framework for the induction of officers into the ICG. The highlights of the policy include induction of women candidates into both Short Service Appointments (SSA) and Permanent Appointments (PA) at par with their male counterparts. SSA has also been opened for male candidates.

The policy ensures equal opportunities for career progression, commencing right from the ab-initio training phase. The existing PA women officers shall also be considered for promotion to higher positions subject to fulfilment of eligibility conditions. The existing serving women officers on SSA will also be provided an option to convert their service to a PA, subject to the fulfilment of stipulated conditions. This progressive step reflects the Government's commitment to Nari Shakti and equal opportunity in the nation's maritime security apparatus.

Streamlined ex-gratia procedures for personnel missing at sea

The second policy reform brings relief and administrative ease to the Next of Kin (NoK) of the personnel who unfortunately go missing at sea in the line of duty. The key highlights of the policy include the authority to declare an ICG personnel missing at sea while on duty as ‘presumed dead’ for the purpose of ex-gratia. The reform significantly eases and accelerates the process for the grant of ex-gratia compensation and terminal benefits to the NoK. This measure ensures that the families of brave personnel are not subjected to prolonged administrative delays during times of mental trauma.

headline: India Leads the Wilderness in Tiger Conservation
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

India Leads the Wilderness in Tiger Conservation

“Protecting Tigers, Preserving Ecosystems”

28 JUL 2026 11:01AM by PIB Delhi

India has emerged as a global leader in tiger conservation through science based policies and strong institutional support. The country is now home to nearly 70% of the world's wild tigers. Technology driven monitoring, effective governance and community participation have strengthened conservation outcomes. India is also advancing global cooperation to secure the future of tigers and their habitats.

Thriving Tigers, Resilient Ecosystems

International Tiger Day, observed every year on 29 July, highlights the global importance of tiger conservation. For India, it reaffirms the Government's long-standing commitment to science-based conservation and sustainable development. The day also showcases India's remarkable conservation achievements. Today, India is home to the world's largest wild tiger population, accounting for nearly 70% of all wild tigers globally. This success reflects decades of sustained policy support, scientific management and community participation, positioning India as a global leader in tiger conservation.

This achievement is rooted in India's deep cultural and ecological connection with the tiger. For centuries, ancient coins, royal seals and temple carvings have portrayed the tiger as a symbol of strength and sovereignty. Recognising this enduring legacy, the Government declared the Royal Bengal Tiger as the National Animal in 1972. Today, the tiger continues to represent India's rich biodiversity, ecological wealth and shared natural heritage across diverse landscapes.

Beyond its cultural significance, the tiger plays a vital ecological role. As an apex predator and umbrella species, it helps maintain healthy forest ecosystems. Conserving tiger habitats protects forests, rivers and countless other species. These forests regulate water, conserve soil, support pollination and moderate local climates. They also reduce disaster risks and provide ecosystem services that sustain rural livelihoods and urban economies. By protecting tigers and their habitats, the Government is strengthening biodiversity conservation, enhancing ecological security and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat through sustainable development.

Did You Know? International Tiger Day traces its origins to the Saint Petersburg Tiger Summit held in November 2010. Leaders from 13 tiger-range countries, including India, adopted the ambitious Tx2 goal to double the global wild tiger population by 2022. Today, it serves as a global platform to review conservation progress, strengthen international cooperation and raise awareness. In 2010, only about 3,200 wild tigers were estimated to remain globally. By 2022, improved conservation and scientific monitoring increased the estimate to around 4,500, with a plausible range of 3,700–5,600 tigers. According to recent global estimates, approximately 5,711 wild tigers remain worldwide, representing an increase of around 78% since 2010.

Rise in the Tiger Numbers: From Crisis to Recovery

India's tiger conservation efforts have emerged as a global model of wildlife recovery. The country has more than doubled its scientifically assessed tiger population since 2006. The All India Tiger Estimation (2022) places India's tiger population at 3,682. The 2022 All India Tiger Estimation covered 20 States and surveyed over 6.41 lakh kilometres on foot. It is among the world's largest and most comprehensive wildlife assessments. This remarkable recovery reflects sustained policy support, science-based conservation and strong institutional governance. Long-term habitat protection, rigorous monitoring and coordinated implementation continue to strengthen tiger conservation across India.

Robust Governance Architecture for Tiger Conservation

India’s policy framework for tiger conservation combines long term vision with sustained institutional support at national and state levels. Project Tiger, the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and Tiger Conservation Plans together provide a robust, science based governance architecture for tiger habitats.

Project Tiger is a flagship Centrally Sponsored Scheme of the Government of India. It is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC). The scheme aims to secure viable tiger populations in their natural habitats. It provides financial and technical assistance to tiger range States for conservation efforts. The programme combines habitat protection, scientific management and regular field based monitoring. This approach has strengthened conservation measures over time.

According to the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) Report (2023), Project Tiger has established a network of 58 tiger reserves across 18 tiger-range States. These reserves cover around 84,500 square kilometres, which is about 2.56% of India's geographical area. Today, Project Tiger remains a cornerstone of India's wildlife conservation efforts and reflects the Government's long term commitment to protecting tigers and their habitats.

Did You Know? Section 38 V (3) of the Wildlife Protection Act, (WPA), 1972 requires every State Government to prepare a Tiger Conservation Plan for each tiger reserve. Such plans must ensure protection of tiger reserves and provide habitat inputs to maintain viable populations of tigers, co predators and prey animals

National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)

NTCA oversees the implementation of Project Tiger and related conservation initiatives. NTCA provides scientific, technical and financial guidance to tiger range States. It approves Tiger Conservation Plans and issues standard operating procedures for reserve management. The Authority also monitors the management of tiger reserves through periodic assessments. Its science based approach improve habitat protection, improves conservation outcomes and supports the long term survival of wild tigers across India.

Did You Know? NTCA is chaired by the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It also includes Members of Parliament, senior government officials and experts. The Authority guides tiger conservation, oversees tiger reserves and ensures effective implementation of Project Tiger across the country.

Tiger Task Force

The Government of India constituted the Tiger Task Force to re-examine conservation policies and recommend reforms. The Tiger Task Force reviewed India's tiger conservation framework and recommended key policy reforms. It brought together administrative experts, ecologists and community representatives. The Task Force emphasised transparency, community participation and stronger institutional support for Project Tiger. Its recommendations shaped a more robust conservation framework. They led to significant amendments to the Wildlife (Protection) Act in 2006. The amendments established the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) and the Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB) as statutory bodies.

India's tiger conservation framework reflects a strong governance model built on institutions and cooperative federalism. This integrated approach is helping secure the future of tigers while advancing India's biodiversity.

Did You Know? India's tiger reserves follow a landscape-based conservation approach. Each reserve includes a Core Area (also known as Critical Tiger Habitat) and a Buffer Area. Core Areas receive the highest level of protection. Buffer Areas balance conservation with sustainable livelihoods. Also, Wildlife corridors connect tiger reserves, enabling safe movement and maintaining healthy tiger populations across landscapes.

Monitoring and Evaluation of Tigers in India

India has developed a robust, science-based system to monitor and evaluate its tiger population. The approach combines field surveys, camera traps, digital technologies and scientific analysis. It generates reliable data on tiger populations, prey species and habitat quality. This information guides evidence-based conservation planning and adaptive management. Continuous monitoring strengthens habitat protection and enables informed management decisions across tiger landscapes.

All India Tiger Estimation (AITE): The World's Largest Biodiversity Survey

AITE is the world's largest biodiversity survey. Conducted every four years, it is led by the NTCA in collaboration with the Wildlife Institute of India (WII). It estimates tiger populations, co-predators, prey species and habitat quality across all tiger bearing States. The 2022 assessment also included India's first nationwide survey of ungulates. The exercise highlighted the importance of healthy prey populations for sustaining viable tiger populations.

Did You Know? The All India Tiger Estimation is recognised as the world's largest biodiversity survey. The NTCA's camera trap survey also holds a Guinness World Record as the world's largest camera trap wildlife survey. Together, advanced technologies and scientific monitoring make India's tiger estimation among the most rigorous in the world.

Technology Driven Monitoring

India has integrated advanced digital technologies into every stage of tiger monitoring. The Monitoring System for Tigers – Intensive Protection and Ecological Status (M-STrIPES) uses GPS, GPRS and remote sensing technologies for field monitoring. GPS tagged photographs improve data accuracy and reduce human error. The platform integrates field observations into a central database for scientific analysis and informed decision making. Artificial intelligence further strengthens monitoring. The Camera Trap Data Repository and Analysis Tool (CaTRAT) automatically classify camera trap images by species. ExtractCompare identifies individual tigers using their unique stripe patterns. Collectively, these tools improve the accuracy and reliability of tiger population estimates.

Management Effectiveness Evaluation (MEE)

The MEE assesses how well tiger reserves are managed. The framework evaluates planning, protection, management processes and conservation outcomes. It helps identify management gaps and reinforce accountability. By 2022, 51 tiger reserves had been evaluated under the framework. Twelve reserves received "Excellent" ratings, while the average management score reached 78%. The findings guide policy decisions, strengthen reserve management and support long-term conservation planning.

India's Global Leadership in Tiger Conservation

India is actively collaborating with countries across the world to strengthen tiger and wildlife conservation. Key partnerships include transboundary biodiversity conservation with Nepal and Bhutan. Collaboration with Myanmar focuses on combating timber trafficking and conserving tigers and other wildlife. India also cooperates with Russia on camera trap data management and through the Indo-Russia Working Sub-Group on Tiger and Leopard Conservation. Partnerships with Botswana, South Africa, Guatemala, Cambodia, Kenya and Namibia strengthen wildlife conservation, management and sustainable biodiversity use. India has also established bilateral cooperation with China on tiger conservation. These partnerships reinforce India's commitment to global wildlife conservation through science, cooperation and shared action.

International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA)

IBCA is a global coalition of 95 big cat range and partner countries, scientific organisations and conservation partners. The Alliance promotes cooperation for conserving seven big cats—tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma. The Union Cabinet approved its establishment on 12 March 2024, with its Secretariat headquartered in India. Building on India's globally recognised tiger conservation experience, the IBCA strengthens international collaboration to protect big cats and their habitats.

Global Tiger Forum (GTF)

GTF is the world's only intergovernmental organisation dedicated exclusively to tiger conservation. Headquartered in New Delhi, it brings together 13 tiger range countries-Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, China, India, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Nepal, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam. The Forum promotes a common approach to conserving tigers, their prey and habitats. It supports landscape-scale conservation, regional capacity building and technological innovation to strengthen tiger conservation across member countries. Through knowledge sharing and international cooperation, the GTF reinforces India's leadership in global tiger conservation.

Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme (ITHCP)

ITHCP is the International Union for Conservation of Nature's (IUCN) flagship tiger conservation initiative. It is funded by the German Government through KfW Development Bank. The programme supports science-based conservation projects across priority tiger landscapes in Asia. It promotes habitat protection, landscape level conservation and international collaboration. India actively participates in ITHCP programmes, strengthening regional efforts to conserve tigers and their habitats.

Did You Know? Conservation Assured Tiger Standards CA|TS is a global certification system that ensures effective management specifically of tiger conservation areas. Launched at the 1st Asian Parks Congress in Japan in 2013. It sets benchmarks for protection, habitat management, community involvement, and wildlife monitoring. CA|TS supports efforts to create safe, sustainable environments for tigers and preserve global biodiversity. CA|TS has accredited 23 Indian tiger reserves ensuring global best practices in conservation.

India's international partnerships are strengthening collective action for tiger conservation across borders. By sharing knowledge, technology and best practices, India continues to advance global efforts to protect tigers and their habitats.

Towards a Secure Future for Tigers

Tiger conservation remains a dynamic and evolving priority for the India. Looking ahead, India’s vision is to secure connected, climate resilient tiger landscapes that support both wildlife and people. Continued investment in data driven monitoring, technology- enabled protection and capacity building of frontline staff will support this vision. Cooperation with other tiger range countries and global partners will also help share knowledge and reinforce collective conservation gains. International Tiger Day offers a recurring opportunity to engage citizens, particularly youth, in this forward looking agenda. By combining strong policy direction with sustained implementation, India aims to keep its tiger conservation journey on a path of global leadership.

headline: Ministry of Civil Aviation inaugurates Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Amritsar
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Ministry of Civil Aviation inaugurates Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Amritsar

Amritsar becomes the second spoke airport under India's International Aviation Hub Strategy

28 JUL 2026 11:00AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Civil Aviation today inaugurated Hub & Spoke International Flight Operations from Amritsar, making it the second airport in the country to be integrated into India's pioneering Hub & Spoke framework for international passenger movement. The inauguration marks the next phase of the Government's strategy to transform India into a global aviation hub by providing seamless international connectivity to passengers from across the country through Indian hub airports.

The launch follows the successful commencement of India's first Hub & Spoke operations from Varanasi on 25 June 2026. Over the past one month, the system has operated smoothly, demonstrating the operational viability of the model and receiving an encouraging response from passengers. During this period, passengers originating from Varanasi have been seamlessly connected through Delhi to eighteen international destinations, validating the effectiveness of the initiative in simplifying international travel.

Through a video message congratulating all the stakeholders present at the Amritsar airport, Union Minister of Civil Aviation Ram Mohan Naidu said, ““Hub & Spoke is not merely an aviation model; it is an opportunity model. Delhi will serve as the hub, while Amritsar will emerge as a major international gateway for Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh. With its strong diaspora connections and vast regional catchment, Amritsar is among the Indian cities that stand to benefit the most from this transformation in global connectivity.”

Amritsar occupies a unique position as one of India's major international gateways, serving pilgrims, members of the Indian diaspora, business travellers and tourists from Punjab and neighbouring regions. Its inclusion under the Hub & Spoke framework is expected to substantially improve access to global destinations through Indian hubs while providing passengers with a faster, more convenient and predictable travel experience.

Emphasizing the larger national vision, the Minister added, “Under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, India is working towards building its own globally competitive aviation hubs. This is not only about improving passenger convenience; it is about strengthening India’s aviation sovereignty and ensuring that Indian hubs connect India to the world.”

Beyond improving passenger experience, the initiative is expected to generate wider economic benefits by strengthening tourism, trade, investment and regional development. Studies undertaken by the Ministry indicate that the development of aviation hub operations could generate nearly 0.4 million direct and indirect jobs and contribute an additional USD 30 billion to India's economy by 2030. By 2047, the cumulative impact is projected to support approximately 16 million direct and indirect jobs while contributing nearly USD 1.4 trillion to the national economy.

With the commencement of operations from Amritsar, international passengers can now complete check-in, immigration and customs formalities at Amritsar before departure. Their baggage will be checked through to the final international destination, enabling them to transfer seamlessly at the designated hub airport to their onward international flight without undergoing immigration or customs formalities again.

Highlighting the transformational impact of the Hub & Spoke model on international connectivity from Amritsar, the Minister said: “Until now, passengers travelling from Amritsar had direct international connectivity to only seven destinations. With the introduction of the Hub & Spoke model, the global connectivity of Delhi Airport will effectively become available to passengers right from Amritsar itself. Travelers will be able to access more than 20 international destinations with a single check-in and a single baggage tag, making the entire journey far more seamless. At present, nearly 1.5 lakh passengers travel from Amritsar to Delhi every year to board international flights, while another 1.5 lakh passengers arrive from overseas via Delhi to reach Amritsar. As travel becomes significantly easier under this integrated system, we expect passenger traffic to grow rapidly.”

The airlines have estimated a potential of nearly 250 passengers per day from Amritsar alone to benefit from the Hub & Spoke model through Delhi. As additional spoke airports are brought under the framework in the coming months, the next phase is expected to facilitate approximately 1,200 passengers every day, equivalent to nearly 4.5 lakh passengers annually, thereby significantly expanding seamless international connectivity from regional India.

The initiative significantly enhances passenger convenience while maintaining the highest standards of security, facilitation and regulatory compliance.

The Hub & Spoke framework forms a key pillar of the Government's International Aviation Hub Strategy, which seeks to strengthen Indian airports as preferred gateways for international travel, improve network efficiency for Indian carriers and reduce dependence on overseas transit hubs. By leveraging India's strategic geographical location and expanding airport infrastructure, the initiative aims to retain a larger share of international transfer traffic within the country while enhancing the competitiveness of India's aviation sector.

The inauguration of Hub & Spoke operations from Amritsar marks another significant milestone in the phased rollout of India's International Aviation Hub Strategy. Additional spoke airports are at advanced stages of operational readiness and will be integrated into the network in a phased manner, creating a nationwide system of seamless international connectivity through Indian hub airports. The initiative represents an important step towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 by building a more connected, efficient and globally competitive aviation ecosystem.

fullText:

Government Strengthens Welfare and Social Security Measures for Senior Citizens Under Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana

Over 8.41 Lakh Senior Citizens Assisted Since Inception FY 2021-22 till date; More Than 7.68 Lakh Beneficiaries Covered Under Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana

28 JUL 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Government of India is implementing a comprehensive range of welfare programmes for senior citizens under the Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) to promote healthy, dignified and active ageing across the country. The details were shared by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, in a written reply to Shri Ganesh Singh in Lok Sabha.

Under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), the Ministry provides grant-in-aid to eligible organisations for operating Senior Citizen Homes, Continuous Care Homes, Mobile Medicare Units and Physiotherapy Clinics. The programme seeks to improve the quality of life of indigent senior citizens by ensuring access to shelter, food, healthcare, recreation and opportunities for active and productive ageing. The Ministry has also prescribed Minimum Standards for Senior Citizen Homes to promote accessible infrastructure and quality care. Since FY 2021-22, the programme has benefitted over 6.98 lakh senior citizens across the country.

The State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) supports State Governments and Union Territory Administrations in implementing State-specific welfare initiatives based on local priorities and requirements. The scheme has been under implementation since FY 2019-20, enabling States and UTs to undertake customised interventions for the welfare of senior citizens.

The Ministry is also implementing the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) to provide free physical aids and assisted living devices to senior citizens suffering from age-related disabilities and having a monthly income of up to ₹15,000. Implemented through the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO), the scheme has benefitted 7,68,749 senior citizens across the country since FY 2021-22, helping restore mobility, independence and improved quality of life.

The Elderline – National Helpline for Senior Citizens (14567), operational from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM every day, provides free information, guidance, emotional support and field intervention in cases of abuse and rescue. Since its dedication to the Nation on 1 October 2021, the helpline has served 8,41,734 senior citizens, offering timely assistance and support across 34 States and Union Territories.

To address the growing demand for skilled elderly care professionals, the Ministry is implementing PM-SPECIAL (System of Providing Elder Care in House and Assisted Living). Since its inception in FY 2023-24, 38,893 geriatric caregivers have been trained, strengthening the country's professional caregiving ecosystem and expanding quality elder care services.

The Government is also promoting innovation in elderly care through the Seniorcare Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) initiative. Under this initiative, eligible start-ups receive equity support of up to ₹1 crore to develop technology-driven solutions for senior citizens. Since its inception, nine start-ups have been supported, encouraging innovation in healthcare, assisted living and age-friendly technologies.

The Government regularly reviews the implementation of AVYAY through stakeholder consultations and independent third-party evaluations to assess emerging needs and improve service delivery. The Ministry further informed that the National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 continues to provide the policy framework for addressing issues relating to healthcare, financial security, assisted living, digital inclusion and active ageing.

The Ministry remains committed to ensuring that senior citizens across the country receive accessible healthcare, social security, rehabilitation support, assisted living services and opportunities for active ageing through a robust network of welfare initiatives, thereby advancing the Government's vision of an inclusive, dignified and age-friendly society.

Over ₹4,276.62 Crores Released Under PM-AJAY Since 2021-22; NITI Aayog Evaluation Highlights Positive Impact on Infrastructure, Education and Livelihoods

3,112 Villages Identified Under Adarsh Gram Component Since 2018-19; Scheme to Continue with Expanded Coverage

28 JUL 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Government continues to strengthen the socio-economic empowerment of Scheduled Caste (SC) communities through the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY).

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment informed the Lok Sabha that an independent evaluation conducted by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog, has found the scheme to be making significant contributions towards improving infrastructure, educational access, livelihood opportunities and the overall quality of life in Scheduled Caste-dominated areas.

In a written reply to Shri Raja A in the Lok Sabha, Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale stated that PM-AJAY, launched in 2021-22, is being implemented through its three components—Adarsh Gram, Grants-in-Aid and Hostels—to accelerate the socio-economic development of Scheduled Caste communities across the country.

The Minister said that since the launch of PM-AJAY, the Central Government has released ₹4,276.62 crores under the scheme up to 2025-26 in 30 states and UTs, while States and Union Territories have reported utilisation of ₹3,185.072 crores towards infrastructure creation, livelihood generation and educational support for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries. During 2025-26 alone, ₹1,100.09 crores have been released under the scheme, reflecting the Government's continued commitment to expanding development interventions.

The Ministry further informed that under the Adarsh Gram component, 3,112 villages have been identified since 2018-19, out of which 3,111 villages in Tamil Nadu have been declared Adarsh Gram, demonstrating substantial progress in developing model villages with improved civic amenities and better public service delivery.

The Development Monitoring And Evaluation Office (DMEO) evaluation concluded that PM-AJAY is well aligned with the Government's objective of inclusive and equitable development. The study found that the scheme has enhanced access to basic infrastructure, electricity, banking facilities, institutional healthcare, education and livelihood opportunities while improving the socio-economic conditions of Scheduled Caste communities in beneficiary villages.

To further strengthen these interventions, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment has proposed the continuation of PM-AJAY from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an enhanced financial outlay. The proposed expansion aims to widen the scheme's coverage, strengthen infrastructure development, create sustainable livelihood opportunities and enhance educational support for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries, ensuring that the benefits of development reach every eligible household.

The Government remains committed to advancing the vision of social justice, inclusive growth and equitable development by empowering Scheduled Caste communities through targeted interventions under PM-AJAY.

headline: India Emerges as World's Second-Largest Supplier of Seafarers
fullText:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

India Emerges as World's Second-Largest Supplier of Seafarers

India's rise from FIFTH place in 2015 to the world's SECOND-largest pool of seafarers in 2026 is a result of the visionary leadership of PM Narendra Modi: Sarbananda Sonowal

India now Contributes 12.16% of the Global Maritime Workforce

Indian officers Constitute 13.41% of the World's officer workforce, reinforcing India's position as a global maritime talent hub

Mission 20% Aims to Make One in every Five Global Seafarers an Indian

28 JUL 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

India has emerged as the world's second-largest supplier of seafarers, contributing 311,936 maritime professionals to the global shipping industry, according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026. The report estimates that India now accounts for 12.16% of the global seafaring workforce, ranking behind only the Philippines and ahead of China, the Russian Federation and Indonesia.

The achievement marks one of the most remarkable transformations in the history of India's maritime sector. In 2015, India contributed only 5.2% of the world's seafarers and ranked fifth globally, behind China, the Philippines, Indonesia and the Russian Federation. Six years later, in 2021, India's share had grown modestly to 6%, though it continued to remain in fifth position. The latest BIMCO-ICS report for 2026, however, records a decisive breakthrough. India's global share has more than doubled over the past decade to 12.16%, propelling the country to second place worldwide and establishing it as one of the world's foremost providers of skilled maritime professionals.

India's strength is particularly evident in the officer cadre. The country now supplies 140,718 officers, accounting for 13.41% of the world's officer workforce, while 171,218 ratings represent 11.29% of the global ratings serving aboard merchant vessels. Overall, Indian seafarers today constitute one of the largest and most skilled maritime workforces supporting global trade.

The report estimates the global supply of seafarers at 2.57 million, while demand has reached 2.55 million, highlighting an increasingly tight global labour market. It also points to a continuing shortage of qualified officers worldwide, positioning India as a critical partner in meeting the shipping industry's future manpower requirements.

India's emergence as a global maritime manpower hub reflects more than a decade of sustained reforms under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Over the past twelve years, the Government has expanded maritime education and skilling, modernised training infrastructure, increased the capacity of maritime training institutes, digitised seafarer certification and regulatory services through the Directorate General of Shipping, strengthened compliance with international Standards of Training, Certification and Watch-keeping (STCW), and enhanced the employability and global competitiveness of Indian seafarers.

Since assuming charge of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways in 2021, Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal has accelerated the reform agenda through the most comprehensive overhaul of India's maritime legal framework in decades. Beginning with the Inland Vessels Act, 2021, the Government has subsequently enacted the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, Indian Ports Act, 2025, Coastal Shipping Act, 2025, Bills of Lading Act, 2025, and the Carriage of Goods by Sea Act, 2025. Collectively, these landmark legislations have modernised maritime governance, strengthened seafarer welfare, aligned India's shipping laws with international conventions, simplified regulatory processes and enhanced ease of doing business across the maritime sector.

Welcoming the report, Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal said, ”India's rise from the fifth-largest supplier of seafarers in 2015 with just 5.2% of the global workforce to the world's second-largest maritime manpower nation with a 12.16% share in 2026 is a story of vision, resolve and transformative leadership. This remarkable turnaround has been made possible under the dynamic leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, whose unwavering commitment over the past twelve years has fundamentally reshaped India's maritime ecosystem. From investing in world-class maritime education and modern training infrastructure to digitising seafarer services, reforming maritime laws and creating globally benchmarked standards, his Government has empowered thousands of young Indians to compete and excel on the world stage. Today's achievement is not merely a statistical milestone, it is a reflection of New India's growing global credibility, the confidence that international shipping companies place in Indian talent, and our collective resolve to establish India as a leading maritime nation."

The Union Minister said the Government is now pursuing Mission 20%, an ambitious national vision to increase India's share of the global seafaring workforce from 12.16% to 20%. "Mission 20% is our next national milestone. We are expanding maritime training capacity, strengthening shipboard training opportunities, fostering deeper industry-academia partnerships, leveraging digital technologies and creating greater opportunities for young Indians, especially women, to pursue rewarding careers at sea. Our vision is clear, to ensure that one in every five seafarers serving aboard merchant ships anywhere in the world is an Indian, recognised globally for professionalism, competence and excellence,” Sonowal added.

With the global shipping industry continuing to face a shortage of qualified officers, India's expanding maritime education ecosystem, internationally recognised training standards and progressive policy framework place the country in a strong position to meet future global demand while advancing the vision of Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.

28 JUL 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

Lakhpati Didi initiative is an outcome of Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme being implemented by Ministry in partnership of States and UTs (except Chandigarh and Delhi), with the objective to improve the livelihoods of poor rural households in country, and organise rural households into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) for their social and financial inclusion.

Lakhpati Didi initiative is to empower and enable Self-Help Groups (SHG) Women, earn a minimum income of Rupees one lakh per annum on a sustainable basis, for at least 4 agricultural seasons and/ or business cycles.

Under the DAY-NRLM, 10.08 crore rural households have been mobilised into around 92 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs) across the country. As on date, more than 3.46 crore SHG members have been enabled as Lakhpati Didis. In Madhya Pradesh, 23,67,520 SHG members have been enabled as Lakhpati Didis, including around 46,000 SHG members in Chhindwara district.

DAY-NRLM is providing entrepreneurship support in the country including Madhya Pradesh, through Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP), a sub-scheme under the DAY-NRLM program that supports and facilitates the SHGs and their family members to set-up small enterprises in the non-farm sector, create an eco-system of entrepreneurship in a block by providing trainings and hand-holding support through the Community Resource Person for Enterprise promotion (CRP-EP), finance through Community Enterprise Fund (CEF), domain and business related mentorship. As of June 2026, 4.32 lakh enterprises have been supported under SVEP in country including 30,573 in Madhya Pradesh.

DAY-NRLM is also providing access to credit and microfinance facilities to empower women through various steps which are as follows:

Funds are provided to SHGs in the form of Revolving Fund (RF) and Community Investment Fund (CIF) to help them in creating a corpus, from which the SHG members can avail loans for various purposes.

The SHGs are also facilitated for Bank linkage for accessing credit at subsidized rates of interest. Since 2013-14, the SHGs have been assisted to access Bank credit of Rs. 13.41 lakh crores, so far.

SHG members are also imparted financial literacy skills through trainings on accounting, record-keeping, budgeting, and loan management etc.

DAY-NRLM also facilitates universal access to cost-effective and reliable financial services to the poor and it works on both demand and supply sides of financial inclusion by promoting financial literacy among the poor and providing catalytic capital to the SHGs and their federations. The promotion of digital finance is done through deployment of SHG Women as Banking Correspondent Sakhi (BC Sakhi), with the support of banks and Common Service Centers.

Under DAY-NRLM, regular trainings and capacity-building programmes are conducted for SHG members and community cadres on SHG management, financial literacy, livelihood promotion and enterprise development to ensure effective implementation of DAY-NRLM across all States.

DAY-NRLM also strengthens market access for SHG products in all States/UTs including Madhya Pradesh through a comprehensive branding and marketing ecosystem. The Ministry has registered the brands “Saras”, “Saras Aajeevika” and “Aajeevika” for promoting SHG products, while 25 States have developed their own State-level brands, such as UMED (Maharashtra), Palash and Adiva (Jharkhand), Himira (Himachal Pradesh) and Mathi (Tamil Nadu).

To further enhance market access, Saras Melas are organised at the National, Regional, State and District levels, including two National-level Saras Melas, one Saras Food Festival and more than 50 State-level Saras Melas every year. The Ministry also operates the Saras Aajeevika Gallery in Central Delhi for the sale of curated SHG products, while several States have established permanent retail outlets under their respective State brands. In addition, the Ministry has developed the eSaras e-commerce platform and partnered with GeM, ONDC, Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho and JioMart to expand market reach and sales opportunities for SHG products.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

Ministry of Rural Development

ALLOCATION OF BUDGET UNDER DDU-GKY

28 JUL 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through placement-linked skilling programs. The cumulative details of funds sanctioned/released and expenditure incurred under DDU-GKY during the last five years and the current year are given in Annexure-I.

Under DDUGKY, a total of 18.45 lakh candidates have been trained, 11.44 lakh candidates have been certified and 12.35 lakh have been placed since inception i.e. 2014-15.

The quality of training and employability are ensured by the scheme design wherein Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) are reimbursed allowable funds only after ensuring 6 months of employment for at least 70% of the trained and certified beneficiaries. Further, an impact assessment study has been conducted through Transrural Agri Consulting Services Pvt. Ltd. in the year 2025. The income enhancement indicator as per the evaluation study has shown that beneficiaries experienced an average salary growth of 30.79% in a period of three years with an average salary of ₹ 16,500 per month.

DDU-GKY incorporates mandatory social inclusion norms to ensure equitable access to training and placement opportunities for disadvantaged groups. The Scheme mandates that 50% of candidates shall be from SC/ST communities, 33% shall be women, and 3% shall be Persons with Disabilities (PwDs).

In order to ensure strengthening skill development, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihood opportunities for rural youth under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY), a number of steps have been taken. These include:

Shifting to Batch-Mode payments in place of the earlier project-mode system, enabling faster and more accountable disbursals.

Greater emphasis has been placed on securing a minimum of 6 months of employment for trained candidates, along with tracking support for 12 months to ensure job continuity. Earlier a minimum of 3 month of employment was mandated.

The scope of the programme has been expanded to include self-employment and emerging gig economy opportunities, promoting entrepreneurial capabilities among the rural youth and encouraging local enterprise development.

headline: VIKSIT GRAM PANCHAYAT PLAN
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

VIKSIT GRAM PANCHAYAT PLAN

28 JUL 2026 6:27PM by PIB Delhi

Under Section 16 of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, every Gram Panchayat is required to prepare a Viksit Gram Panchayat Plan (VGPP) through a participatory planning process. The Gram Sabha identifies and prioritises the permissible works required for the holistic development of the Gram Panchayat, and the Gram Panchayat prepares the VGPP in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The approved VGPP is thereafter consolidated at the Intermediate and District Panchayat levels for preparation of the aggregate Block and District Plans under the Mission. Yuktdhara is a GIS-based planning support tool that assists authorised functionaries in scientific planning by providing geospatial information and analytical inputs for the identification, prioritisation and planning of permissible works, thereby supporting the preparation of the VGPP. Access to the Yuktdhara portal is provided to authorised functionaries designated by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations in accordance with the prescribed operational framework.

As per Section 21 of the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, the State Government is responsible for providing the necessary staff and technical support, including Rozgar Sahayaks and Computer Operators, to the District Programme Coordinator and the Programme Officer for the effective implementation of the Programme. These matters such as the manner by which the rozgar sahayaks and computer operators work fall within the administrative domain of the respective States/Union Territories.

The Ministry accords high priority to capacity building of all stakeholders for effective implementation of VB–G RAM G. Training programmes are being organised at the National, State, District, Block and Gram Panchayat levels through a cascading training framework covering the preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans (VGPPs), technology-enabled planning and monitoring tools including use of Yuktdhara. Detailed training modules, user manuals, standard operating procedures and digital learning resources like e-Saksham have also been made available with the States/Union Territories to facilitate effective implementation and strengthen participatory planning through Gram Sabhas. Also, Capacity Building is an ongoing process and as per the needs and requirements of the States/UTs the technical tram send by the Ministry to the respective States/UTs.

Under the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G, Mates engaged under the Scheme are paid wages at the semi-skilled wage rate, as notified by the respective State Government/Union Territory Administration in accordance with the applicable wage notifications. The wage rates payable to Mates are determined by the respective State Governments/Union Territory Administrations.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.
